subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action through session_status, or should model-originated compaction remain unavailable until a different policy boundary exists?
rationale: The implementation shape can be narrow, but the core choice is a trust boundary: a model tool call would intentionally abort, compact, and resume active session state without an authorized sender command.

options.title: Approve narrow self-compaction
options.body: Allow a current-session-only session_status compact action after the open PR is rebased and its security/runtime proof is refreshed.

options.title: Require an explicit policy gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require an operator or tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer to continuation design
options.body: Do not land the narrow PR and decide self-compaction only as part of a broader continuation API.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-compaction
recommendation.body: Allow a current-session-only session_status compact action after the open PR is rebased and its security/runtime proof is refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across session_status, mutation tracking, gateway actions, and the admin compaction boundary.
